record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: For each integer d ≥ 3, let r(d) be the smallest positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization of the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d such that the union of any r(d) distinct 1-factors is connected. What is the value of r(d)?

evidence.quote: Question 2.1 (Behague, [1]). For each d ∈ N with d ≥ 3, let r = r(d) be the minimal positive integer such that there exists a 1-factorization M of Qd where the union of any r distinct 1-factors is connected. What is the value of r(d)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer d ≥ 1, let Q_d denote the d-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is {0,1}^d and whose edges join pairs of vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate. A 1-factor of Q_d is a perfect matching of Q_d, and a 1-factorization of Q_d is a partition of its edge set into 1-factors (necessarily d of them, since Q_d is d-regular). Given a 1-factorization M = {F_1, …, F_d} and a subset S ⊆ M, the union ⋃_{F ∈ S} F is regarded as a spanning subgraph of Q_d.

For each integer d ≥ 3, define r(d) to be the smallest positive integer r with the following property: there exists a 1-factorization M of Q_d such that for every subset S ⊆ M with |S| = r, the spanning subgraph ⋃_{F ∈ S} F is connected.

Determine r(d).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open in the sense that the exact value of r(d) is not known. Lower bound r(d) ≥ 3 follows from results on perfect 1-factorizations (Laufer). Behague gave an upper bound r(d) ≤ ⌈d/2⌉ + 1, and a 2025 preprint "Connecting hypercube 1-factors" (arXiv:2508.15698) improves this to r(d) = O(log d) via a randomized construction. It is conjectured that r(d) could be as small as 3 (or constant), but this is not established.

status_evidence.title: Connecting hypercube 1-factors
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a 1-factorisation of Q_d such that the union of any Ω(log d) 1-factors is connected, improving the previous ⌈d/2⌉+1 bound of Behague.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound improved to O(log d); exact value of r(d) still unknown.

status_evidence.title: Semi-perfect 1-Factorizations of the Hypercube
status_evidence.snippet: Related work on 1-factorizations of Q_d with connectivity-type properties.
status_evidence.claim: Background showing the problem context and that perfect 1-factorizations do not exist for Q_d with d>2.

status_evidence.title: A collection of open problems (Leader 60)
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as an open question.
